steps.text: About four thousand years ago, a king in the Indus Valley was carved wearing a cloak of three-leaf patterns. Was that cloth printed with a carved block? Nobody knows.
steps.say: About four thousand years ago, a king in the Indus Valley was carved wearing a cloak of three-leaf patterns. Was that cloth printed with a carved block? Nobody knows.

steps.text: This is The Repeating Hand: an open-data history of block printing, the oldest way to copy a pattern. Every claim carries its source.
steps.say: This is The Repeating Hand: an open-data history of block printing, the oldest way to copy a pattern. Every claim carries its source.

steps.text: Meet the Priest-King in three-D, rebuilt from museum photographs. Turn him around, then switch the stone to printed cloth. That is an illustration of the idea, not evidence.
steps.say: Meet the Priest-King in three-D, rebuilt from museum photographs. Turn him around, then switch the stone to printed cloth. That is an illustration of the idea, not evidence.

steps.text: Then follow the craft across the map: the first cotton at Mehrgarh, carved blocks in Egypt, Indian cottons found in Cairo, and the calico that changed Europe.
steps.say: Then follow the craft across the map: the first cotton at Mair-gar, carved blocks in Egypt, Indian cottons found in Cairo, and the calico that changed Europe.

steps.text: Every claim is sorted by how well it holds up: evidenced, reported, not found, or imagined. Nothing is passed off as settled.
steps.say: Every claim is sorted by how well it holds up: evidenced, reported, not found, or imagined. Nothing is passed off as settled.

steps.text: And it is free and open source. The code, the data and the three-D model are all in a public GitHub repo. Fork it, reuse it, and tell a different history.
